hyperedges.label: Three Tests, Three Different Questions (Validation Battery)
Exclude Contaminating Covariates/Periods to Sharpen the Causal Estimate

nodes.label: Causal Impact Campaign Skill
nodes.rationale: Encodes hard-won lessons from real client engagements around short campaigns, retail seasonality, and honest statistical communication; runs two independent Bayesian methods for robustness plus a validation suite.

nodes.label: Multi-Method Analysis
nodes.rationale: No single method is perfect for observational causal inference; each has different assumptions and blind spots, so cross-method agreement is more convincing than any single p-value.

nodes.label: BSTS (tfcausalimpact)
nodes.rationale: Primary analysis; decomposes the series into trend + seasonality + regression and projects a counterfactual; struggles with short campaigns where daily variance overwhelms the signal.

nodes.label: CausalPy
nodes.rationale: Robustness check with a different inference engine (NUTS/HMC); no time series structure; uses posterior predictions (observed - counterfactual) after fixing an early coefficient-parsing bug.

nodes.label: RDiT (Regression Discontinuity in Time)
nodes.rationale: Local linear regression at the intervention boundary; best method for short campaigns (<7 days); the only bug-independent baseline when its bandwidth window does not overlap a masked period.

nodes.label: Conformal Prediction Intervals
nodes.rationale: Distribution-free intervals from pre-period residual quantiles; ~61% tighter than Bayesian CIs; a sanity check on Bayesian CI width (2x wider => overconfident model).

nodes.label: Covariate Safety Audit
nodes.rationale: A covariate correlated with both the outcome and the intervention absorbs the causal effect, biasing toward zero; baseline must be the last 7 days of the pre-period, not the full mean; flags INCLUDE/CAUTION/SKIP.

nodes.label: Multi-Modal Holiday Intensity (xmas_intensity)
nodes.rationale: Binary sale flags cannot capture magnitude (Black Friday is ~5x a normal sale day); a 6-component Gaussian curve reaches r=0.828 with revenue vs r~0.02 for a binary winter_sale_flag.

nodes.label: Specification Curve Analysis (SCA)
nodes.rationale: A 440-spec sweep (55 covariate bundles x 8 infra combos) tests all analytical forking paths rather than one cherry-picked p-value; the grid is the strongest single signal because it does not share single-spec failure modes.

nodes.label: Pre-Period Placebo Test / FPR Calibration
nodes.rationale: In-time placebo; the single most diagnostic BSTS validation; a well-calibrated model has FPR~5%, but all tested methods show 35-55% naive per-window FPR on daily retail revenue - a high FPR means distrust a single naive interval, not that the result is unreliable.

nodes.label: Rolling-Backtest Empirical-Null Rank
nodes.rationale: The miscalibration-immune headline statistic: effect-size ranking of the real effect against an empirical null of rolling-window placebos is unaffected by systematic interval under-coverage.

nodes.label: Date-Shuffled Randomization Test
nodes.rationale: An optional secondary cross-check (a misnomer for a true permutation test); on autocorrelated/masked series it often tests the wrong question - training-window length is a first-order confounder, so it is conservative rather than calibrated.

nodes.label: Masking High-Variance Pre-Periods
nodes.rationale: Masking winter sale windows preserves the annual cycle while removing noise (CV 58%->24%); a data-prep decision more defensible than spec search, but you MUST verify the mask reaches the model input as a true removal, not a zero-fill.

nodes.label: Data-Prep Zero-Injection Trap
nodes.rationale: A mask that drops rows followed by a prep_df that reindexes to a continuous daily index and fills y=0 + interpolated covariates teaches BSTS a spurious 'winter<->$0' relationship; discovered as Issue #51; affects every method that consumes the prepped frame except RDiT (when its bandwidth avoids the mask).

nodes.label: tfcausalimpact p-value Formula
nodes.rationale: Verified from causalimpact/inferences.py compute_p_value: two-sided min(upper_tail,lower_tail)/(N+1) over post-period sums - a posterior predictive p-value, NOT a frequentist Type-I rate; clusters around 0.5 under composite nulls.

nodes.label: Probability of Direction (prob_positive)
nodes.rationale: 1-p framing ('87% probability positive') resonates with non-technical stakeholders and is grounded under uniform priors; but converting a cherry-picked p to a probability smuggles bias into a Bayesian-sounding claim.

nodes.label: Claim Framing Guide
nodes.rationale: From adversarial review: distinguish confirmatory (pre-registered) from exploratory (post-hoc) results; lead with the Bayesian posterior across ALL specs and direction consistency, never the cherry-picked p-value; the client needs to know whether to run the promo again, not p<0.05.

nodes.label: Diagnose, Don't Demote
nodes.rationale: When model-p passes but a placebo test fails, run two cheap Cloud Run diagnostics (training-length-matched permutation + mask-off rolling placebo, ~$0.10) before rewriting client framing; spec-shopping to a passing spec is p-hacking (garden of forking paths).

nodes.label: Subtract Before You Add (Meta-Lesson)
nodes.rationale: The biggest improvements come from removing contaminated covariates and high-variance pre-periods, not adding features; three of five improvement steps in the canonical engagement were subtractions.

nodes.label: VI Stochasticity Warning
nodes.rationale: Variational inference is non-deterministic even with a fixed seed; single-run p differences of +-0.04 are noise; use HMC (deterministic given seed) or average 5+ VI runs for definitive A/B comparisons.

nodes.label: Identification Assumptions
nodes.rationale: A write-up without enumerated identification assumptions is a prediction document mislabeled; the 6-item set: sharp intervention, SUTVA in time, covariate exogeneity, regime stationarity, mask non-informativeness, randomization-test exchangeability.

nodes.label: Interactive HTML Explorer
nodes.rationale: The highest-impact deliverable: a single self-contained HTML file with Plotly.js and embedded pre-computed data that lets the client explore robustness themselves across specs rather than trusting a static summary.

nodes.label: Signal-to-Noise Ratio Assessment
nodes.rationale: Early SNR = expected_daily_effect / daily_std sets client expectations: SNR<0.2 is very unlikely to reach p<0.10, so warn upfront on short volatile campaigns.

nodes.label: Fake p-values in Multi-Method Pipelines
nodes.rationale: Never fill placeholder p-values for methods that do not produce them (CausalPy posterior, conformal intervals); return p=None and display N/A so a scorecard does not falsely read '4 methods agree'.

nodes.label: Comparison vs Alternatives
nodes.rationale: Positions the skill against Google CausalImpact (R), tfcausalimpact, Meta GeoLift, and CausalPy; the differentiators are multi-method validation, covariate safety audit, permutation testing, and FPR calibration.

nodes.label: Companion & Related Skills
nodes.rationale: Names data-provenance-verifier, cloud-run-batch-experiment, and client-proposal-slide as companions; permutation-validation and bsts-placebo-calibration were merged into this skill in v2.0.0.

nodes.label: The Journey: p~0.22 to p<0.05
nodes.rationale: Every causal analysis follows the pattern of a promising-but-not-significant first result then systematic improvements; the masking breakthrough (excluding high-variance winter sale periods) was the single biggest improvement.

nodes.label: Case Study: Path to a Validated Result
nodes.rationale: From p=0.22 to a spec-curve-validated effect; the honest validation comes from three complementary signals - the 224-spec grid, the rolling-placebo backtest rank 0.94, and the date-shuffled randomization test with a training-length-matched diagnostic.
nodes.norm_label: case study: path to a validated result

nodes.label: Issue #51 Mask Zero-Injection Fix
nodes.rationale: A mask-aware index filter narrowed the CI 26% and tightened p 4x (0.047->0.005); the pre-fix p=0.047 was computed on a silently corrupted pre-period where masked days were reinjected as $0 revenue (fixed in PR #52).

nodes.label: 224-Spec Robustness Grid
nodes.rationale: 208/208 valid specs directional positive, top 10 per mask mode $199K-$226K with model p<0.025; becomes the primary validation for the client headline because it does not share single-spec failure modes (16 degenerate log-target specs filtered first).

nodes.label: Demo Output: 20mph Speed Limit Policy Impact Card
nodes.rationale: A warm-editorial single-card summary deliverable (DM Serif Display + Manrope): verdict badge, three stat boxes (-23 acc/day, 97.2% probability, p=0.028), a dual-method agreement column, a key-modelling-decisions column, and a validation footer (backtests, placebo, cross-method).
nodes.norm_label: demo output: 20mph speed limit policy impact card

nodes.label: Techniques That Worked
nodes.rationale: Catalog of validated techniques: combined covariate safety audit, masked pre-periods (post-Issue-#51 fix), high-variance exclusion, multi-modal holiday intensity, RDiT, conformal CIs, effect decomposition, weather covariates, rolling-placebo backtest, 224-spec grid, training-length-matched date-shuffled test.

nodes.label: Techniques That Didn't Work (and Why)
nodes.rationale: Catalog of failures: Fourier annual seasonality (needs 2+ cycles), sin/cos DoW (redundant with nseasons=7), WeightedSumFitter (wrong model class), Google Trends brand search (endogenous), date-shuffled randomization on the canonical spec (structural, not a model defect), p-value comparison in permutation, unfiltered log-target on short masked pre-periods.

nodes.label: Covariate Correlation Benchmarks
nodes.rationale: Retail benchmarks: organic_sessions (r=0.86) is the safest control; paid_sessions (r=0.89) needs a contamination check; xmas_intensity r=0.828; winter_sale_flag r=-0.02 is inadequate for retail peaks - benchmarks, not universals.

nodes.label: Pre-Period Start Date & Masking Sensitivity
nodes.rationale: Jan 6 post-Christmas start gives -27% CI; mask Nov-Jan both years gives -64% CI; pre-periods <60 days produce overconfident results; always verify temporal scope covers all seasonal instances.

nodes.label: Leave-One-Out Covariate Sensitivity
nodes.rationale: More covariates is not always better; cos_dow was noise (nseasons=7 already captures weekly seasonality) so the model improves without it, while organic_sessions is critical (model collapses to p=0.148 without it).

nodes.label: prepare_model_data (data prep function)
nodes.rationale: Reindexes to a continuous daily index then fillna(0) on the target and linear-interpolates covariates - the exact pattern that produces the zero-injection trap when applied after a date mask.

nodes.label: christmas_proximity (Gaussian holiday curve)
nodes.rationale: Continuous Gaussian bell peaking near Black Friday (~27 days before Christmas) with a Boxing Day tail; implements the multi-modal holiday intensity covariate.

nodes.label: GA4 Features Table SQL
nodes.rationale: BigQuery SQL that derives daily revenue, transactions, sessions, and paid/organic session+revenue splits from GA4 events, plus a dim_calendar with Easter/Black Friday logic.

nodes.label: Validation Suite (backtest / placebo code)
nodes.rationale: extract_metrics + backtest_metrics (WAPE, RMSE, coverage_95) + rolling backtest window generation + placebo_rank = (placebo_effects < real_effect).mean().

nodes.label: Interactive HTML Explorer Template
nodes.rationale: Single self-contained HTML with 5 sections (hero+spec selector, counterfactual chart, method comparison, decomposition, channel/persistence) driven by an embedded const DATA object and Plotly.js patterns.

nodes.label: numpy Version Conflict (tfcausalimpact vs CausalPy)
nodes.rationale: tfcausalimpact needs numpy<2 (TensorFlow 2.16) and CausalPy needs numpy>=2 (PyMC/PyTensor); they cannot coexist in one process - run tfcausalimpact first, then upgrade numpy and run CausalPy in a separate script.

nodes.label: CausalPy macOS cores=1 Fix
nodes.rationale: The default multiprocessing fork on macOS raises a RuntimeError during bootstrapping; set cores=1 in sample_kwargs.

nodes.label: Open-Meteo Weather API
nodes.rationale: Best free source for daily temperature/precipitation covariates (no API key); backfill recent days from the forecast API; use curl -sk to bypass corporate SSL proxies.

nodes.label: CausalPy Short-Window Misdiagnosis
nodes.rationale: The xarray "Dimension(s) 'draw','chain' do not exist" error is the v0.4+ InferenceData API change, not a short-window bug; the three-bug wrapper fix (InferenceData unwrap + pre-period z-score + post-window upper bound) makes CausalPy run cleanly on 4-day windows.

nodes.label: Eval Suite (Assertion->Source Mapping)
nodes.rationale: Paper-to-assertion mapping grounding each eval assertion (methodology, validation, covariates, interpretation, client framing, edge cases) in 15 academic papers + 3 industry tools.

nodes.label: Effect Decomposition
nodes.rationale: Separate CausalImpact runs on conversion_rate, aov, and transactions reveal which lever the campaign pulled; the 'conversion barrier removal' pattern (CR up, AOV flat) directly informs future offer design.

nodes.label: Channel Split (paid vs organic)
nodes.rationale: Run CausalImpact on paid_revenue and organic_revenue separately (organic_sessions as control for both) to distinguish a site-wide conversion effect from a channel-specific traffic effect.

nodes.label: Post-Promo Persistence
nodes.rationale: persistence_ratio = post-promo avg daily effect / during-promo avg daily effect; unreliable for short campaigns and highly sensitive to covariate choice, so frame as inconclusive unless multiple specs agree.

nodes.label: Weather Covariate
nodes.rationale: Low standalone revenue correlation (r ~ -0.05..+0.03) but an orthogonal exogenous signal that tightens CIs 2-5% and is the single biggest permutation-discrimination improver.

nodes.label: Prophet Cross-Validation
nodes.rationale: An independent model family (additive Fourier seasonality + changepoint trend) for high-stakes claims; produces no frequentist p-value, so report 'CI excludes zero' when actual_sum - yhat_upper_sum > 0.

nodes.label: Contaminated Exogenous Metrics (Brand Search Endogeneity)
nodes.rationale: Brand search is endogenous (the promo drives search) and worsened p ~3x; the correlation paradox - category-level Trends has near-zero revenue correlation (~0.01) but is the best covariate because it is exogenous and adds daily variation without redundancy.

nodes.label: Sale Period Auto-Detection (Coupon Ratio)
nodes.rationale: A bidirectional MAD z-score on the coupon ratio classifies coupon vs sitewide sales; both sale covariates must be zeroed during the treatment window (ADR 0020) - unzeroed p=0.074 vs zeroed p=0.033.

nodes.label: Tiered Covariate Recommendation
nodes.rationale: Default (5 base) -> Enhanced (+category Trends) -> Full (+sale signals), each permutation-validated; use permutation p<0.10 as the gatekeeper, not an arbitrary covariate cap.

nodes.label: Brodersen et al. (2015)
nodes.rationale: Inferring causal impact using Bayesian structural time-series models (Annals of Applied Statistics); the foundational BSTS/CausalImpact paper.

nodes.label: Scott & Varian (2014)
nodes.rationale: Predicting the present with Bayesian structural time series; covariates must be predictive, not causal (unaffected by treatment).

nodes.label: Abadie et al. (2010)
nodes.rationale: Synthetic control methods (JASA); established the in-space placebo test and the post/pre MSPE ratio (an effect-size statistic, not a model p-value).

nodes.label: Abadie et al. (2015)
nodes.rationale: Comparative politics and the synthetic control method (AJPS); introduced the in-time placebo test.

nodes.label: Abadie (2021)
nodes.rationale: Using synthetic controls (J. Economic Literature); canonical definitions, exclusion zone around the real intervention, more pre-period = lower bias.

nodes.label: Eggers et al. (2024)
nodes.rationale: Placebo tests for causal inference (AJPS); FPR=5% defines a well-calibrated test and identifies the null-hacking threat.

nodes.label: Young (2019)
nodes.rationale: Channeling Fisher (QJE); model p-values inflate under misspecification and effect-size/randomization ranking is robust to the interval miscalibration that inflates naive p-values.

nodes.label: Linden (2018)
nodes.rationale: Using permutation tests to enhance causal inference in interrupted time series (J. Eval Clin Pract); ITS permutation compares the magnitude of trend changes across pseudo-treatments.

nodes.label: Athey & Imbens (2017)
nodes.rationale: The state of applied econometrics (J. Economic Perspectives); endorses placebo analyses as a standard robustness requirement for observational causal inference.

nodes.label: Gils et al. (2022)
nodes.rationale: Evaluating the power of the causal impact method (BMC Infectious Diseases); BSTS FDR inflates to ~10% with 6 pre-period observations and recovers to ~5% with 12+.

nodes.label: Peduzzi et al. (1996)
nodes.rationale: Events-per-variable simulation study (J. Clinical Epidemiology); EPV<10 causes unreliable significance tests - the basis for the short-pre-period-plus-many-covariates overfit warning.

nodes.label: Makowski et al. (2019)
nodes.rationale: Indices of effect existence and significance in the Bayesian framework (Frontiers in Psychology); formalized the Probability of Direction (pd) metric.

nodes.label: Gelman, Meng & Stern (1996)
nodes.rationale: Posterior predictive assessment via realized discrepancies (Statistica Sinica); the canonical posterior-predictive-check framework of which tfcausalimpact's compute_p_value is an instance.

nodes.label: Phipson & Smyth (2010)
nodes.rationale: Permutation p-values should never be zero; justification for the (k+1)/(N+1) Monte-Carlo correction used by tfcausalimpact internally and by the permutation aggregator.

nodes.label: Simonsohn, Simmons & Nelson (2020)
nodes.rationale: Specification curve analysis (Nature Human Behaviour); the canonical three-step SCA - claim 'Simonsohn-validated' only if the bootstrap joint inference test is run.

nodes.label: Fisher (1935)
nodes.rationale: The Design of Experiments; historical origin of randomization inference - any test statistic is valid for permutation, but effect-size statistics are power-optimal for magnitude alternatives.

nodes.label: Gelman & Carlin (2014)
nodes.rationale: Beyond power calculations: Type S (sign) and Type M (magnitude) errors; for low-power single-unit short-window studies these matter more than Type-I.

nodes.label: Blei, Kucukelbir & McAuliffe (2017)
nodes.rationale: Variational Inference: A Review for Statisticians (JASA); VI underestimates posterior variance, making CIs too narrow and posterior predictive p-values too small - prefer HMC for headline results.

nodes.label: Hyndman & Athanasopoulos (2021)
nodes.rationale: Forecasting: Principles and Practice (rolling-origin CV); treats rolling-origin CV as a forecast-accuracy tool, not a placebo significance test - citing it to justify 'backtest as primary placebo' is a category error.

nodes.label: Lakens (2017)
nodes.rationale: Equivalence tests (TOST); to claim 'no meaningful effect' you must test against a smallest effect of interest with adequate power - a non-significant interval alone cannot support 'it didn't work'.

nodes.label: Marsman & Wagenmakers (2016)
nodes.rationale: Three insights from a Bayesian interpretation of the one-sided p value; under uniform priors the one-sided p equals the posterior mass below zero, grounding the 1-p = prob_positive conversion.

nodes.label: CI Test Workflow (npm test on Node 20/22)
nodes.rationale: GitHub Actions workflow running npm test on push and pull_request to main across a Node.js 20/22 matrix.
nodes.norm_label: ci test workflow (npm test on node 20/22)

nodes.label: Interactive Causal Impact Report (Retail Delivery Promo)
nodes.rationale: Warm-editorial, verdict-first report UI: serif display headline stating the estimated effect, significance badge, an interactive model-specification dropdown, colored-border metric cards, and a counterfactual explainer section.
nodes.norm_label: interactive causal impact report (retail delivery promo)

nodes.label: £XXXk Incremental Revenue Estimate
nodes.rationale: Headline finding: ~22% higher than predicted over 4 promo days; £74K/day average uplift.

nodes.label: Model Specification Selector
nodes.rationale: Interactive dropdown lets the reader explore how results change across model specifications, making the report an explorable deliverable rather than a static one.

nodes.label: Enhanced Model Spec (excl. Xmas & paid_sessions)
nodes.rationale: Recommended specification: excludes Christmas distortion and the contaminated paid_sessions covariate; pre-period anchored at Jan 6 2025; produces the significant £XXXk estimate (p<0.05).

nodes.label: BSTS Significance (p=0.039)
nodes.rationale: Bayesian Structural Time Series result: statistically significant at p<0.05, 96.1% probability the effect is positive.

nodes.label: Counterfactual Analysis (What would have happened without the promo)
nodes.rationale: Bayesian models trained on pre-campaign data predict expected revenue; the gap between predicted and observed is the estimated causal effect.
nodes.norm_label: counterfactual analysis (what would have happened without the promo)

nodes.label: Contaminated paid_sessions Covariate (excluded)
nodes.rationale: paid_sessions was excluded from the recommended model because it was contaminated and would bias the causal estimate.

nodes.label: Policy Impact Report Card (20 mph Speed Limit Rollout)
nodes.rationale: Compact executive report card: green SIGNIFICANT verdict badge, three headline metric tiles (reduction, probability, p-value), a dual-method agreement panel, a key-modelling-decisions list, and a validation footer (backtests/placebo/cross-method).

nodes.label: 20 mph Speed Limit Rollout Policy Impact
nodes.rationale: Feb 3-28 2026, daily accident count; estimated reduction of 23 accidents/day, 97.2% probability of effect, p=0.028.
nodes.norm_label: 20 mph speed limit rollout policy impact

nodes.label: Dual-Method Agreement
nodes.rationale: Two independent methods agree on direction and magnitude, strengthening the causal claim.

nodes.label: tfcausalimpact (BSTS)
nodes.rationale: Bayesian Structural Time Series estimate: -23 acc/day, p=0.028.

nodes.label: CausalPy (RDiT)
nodes.rationale: Regression-Discontinuity-in-Time estimate: -26 acc/day, p=0.019.

nodes.label: Key Modelling Decisions
nodes.rationale: Excluded school holiday period (CI width reduced 19%); removed construction_zones covariate (was absorbing 8 accidents/day of effect); added rainfall + daylight hours (multi-modal curve, r=0.791).

nodes.label: Removed construction_zones Covariate
nodes.rationale: construction_zones was removed because it was absorbing ~8 accidents/day of the treatment effect, masking the true reduction.

nodes.label: Validation Suite (backtests / placebo / cross-method)
nodes.rationale: Robustness footer: 3 backtests passed, 1 placebo passed, cross-method validated.
